newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: London Club to delay talks with Yugoslavia - paper.
newsitem.headline: London Club to delay talks with Yugoslavia - paper.

text.p: Talks between Yugoslavia and its London Club creditors will not start until Belgrade supplements its reports outlining economic policy to the year 2005, the daily Nasa Borba said on Tuesday.

"The federal government had fallen into an old trap of inflating gross domestic product (GDP) in its economic report prepared for the club," the paper quoted a source in the Yugoslav central bank as saying.
According to official estimates, Yugoslavia's GDP stands at around $15.5 billion. Independent IEN Institute of Economic Sciences warned earlier the true value of GDP hardly exceeded $10 billion.
The unnamed central bank expert said an unrealistically high GDP would place Yugoslavia in a group of countries not qualifying for facilities which Belgrade seeks.

"On the other hand, the National Bank of Yugoslavia has done its part of the job well and there were no objections to the reports provided by NBY," Nasa Borba quoted its unnamed London source as saying.

Yugoslavia's chief negotiator with the club and federal minister without portfolio Vuk Ognjanovic last week said a deal with the London Club was possible without Belgrade regulating its status in the IMF first.
He said talks with the club would be resumed by the end of November.
